memory_bridge: The prime minister’s shoe retrieves title-reading シュ; the neck fitted into a cubby retrieves standalone Kun くび.

readings.editorial_reason: Promoted because 首相（しゅしょう）is common, modern, and pedagogically useful.
readings.overlay: The head of government puts on a formal shoe before appearing as 首相（しゅしょう）; shoe → シュ.

readings.editorial_reason: Promoted because 首（くび）is common, modern, and pedagogically useful.
readings.overlay: A cubby-shaped collar snaps around the neck beneath the face: cubby → くび, the standalone 首（くび）.

readings.editorial_reason: Promoted because 也 is a common modern anchor for this distinct reading.
readings.overlay: The hooked last stroke reaches out to pull one more guest into the group: 也（yě）, “also.” Let yě dip low, then curl upward like the hook.
